content.comment_body: Hello, I want to connect my [product_name] with an incremental encoder that uses I/O Link. Is it possible to achieve this connection?

No. The [product_name] [article_no] is not compatible with I/O Link. It only supports Ethernet TCP/IP with the S7 protocol, and starting from [product_name] [version_no], Modbus TCP/IP is available as well.

I understand, but I'm wondering if connecting the signal wires directly to the controller could work. The encoder's specifications mention an I/O Link interface—do you think this could be successful? Here is my encoder: [url]
I'm not certain about that, but personally I wouldn't recommend trying it.
That approach won't be effective. You need an IO-Link master with Modbus TCP capability. Additionally, it seems your [product_name] may not be suitable for this encoder.
So, if I use something like the AL1340 IO-Link, could my [product_name] connect to the encoder and everything would function properly?

There's no information about what you plan to achieve with the [product_name] and encoder. Who can answer your last question without further details? Why use an encoder with IO-Link? You could also choose encoders with Modbus TCP/IP. It may even turn out that the [product_name] isn't the best controller for your application—you can find controllers with IO-Link compatibility, avoiding the need for a converter. Please share more details about your application and what components you already have. Sometimes it's better to change components for a more cost-effective solution. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Forum users are trying to integrate a [product_name] module with an incremental encoder that uses I/O-Link communication. The conversation reveals that the [product_name] does not support I/O-Link natively and lacks official documentation or established solutions for combining these devices. This mismatch in protocol support is causing confusion and stopping users from achieving integration with their existing hardware setup.
analysis.user_expectations: Users hope to directly connect and establish communication between their [product_name] and the encoder, preferably by wiring the encoder’s output to the controller or using a simple interface module.
